title: The Hands That Care for You
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
A song is sung in Proverbs' end
Of hands that worked with love,
That kneaded bread and smoothed the sheets
And thanked the Lord above.

[Chorus]
So thank the hands that care for you,
And lend your own two, too;
For loving, helping hands are how
A home is warm and true.

[Verse 2]
She spoke with kind and gentle words,
Her heart was brave and strong;
She reached her hand out to the poor
And hummed a working song.

[Chorus]

[Verse 3]
Her children rose and called her blessed,
They loved her very much;
For every meal and mended sock
And every gentle touch.

[Chorus]

[Verse 4]
So close your eyes, my little one,
Two hands are holding you;
And in the morning you can help
With your two small hands too.

[Chorus]
mood: Working music, slowed all the way down to bedtime. A gentle rocking pulse under the voice - the rhythm of hands doing the same kind thing over and over, folding, stirring, smoothing a blanket flat. Fingerpicked guitar circling one small figure, with a warm low note underneath that arrives on every second line like a hand resting on a shoulder. It travels from busy to still, so the last verse feels like the day's work being set down for the night.
